stories.title: Bill C-9 Passes House — Now in Senate
stories.summary: Bill C-9 (Combatting Hate Act) passed third reading 188-144. Creates new Criminal Code offences for hate symbol display and 100m exclusion zones around religious institutions. NDP + CPC voted against. CCLA warns it threatens rights of every Canadian. Canadian Labour Congress raised concerns about criminalizing peaceful protest. Now at second reading in Senate.
stories.connection: Directly connected to CIJA lobbying (73 contacts during JUST committee review). Investigation Leviathan Layer 1.

stories.title: MAID Mental Illness Expansion Set for March 2027
stories.summary: One year until MAID expands to people whose sole condition is mental illness. Alberta proposing legislation to eliminate Track 2 MAID entirely + prohibit MAID for mental illness, mature minors, and advance requests. Joint parliamentary committee required by Feb 28, 2026.
stories.connection: Connected to MAID death count (76,475 cumulative, tracking to 100K by June 2026). Site homepage statistic.

stories.title: Carney Meeting Brookfield Executives Despite Ethics Screen
stories.summary: Reports indicate PM Carney met with Brookfield executives despite ethics screen. Screen administered by his own chief of staff. ETHI committee learned screen administrators do not know specific fund assets. Democracy Watch calls it loophole-filled smokescreen.
stories.connection: Direct update to carney_conflicts_dossier.json. Charges sheet: Carney at severity 3 (CRITICAL CoIA finding).

stories.title: Alberta CorruptCare Scandal — RCMP Investigation
stories.summary: AHS CEO Mentzelopoulos alleges Smith government fired her 2 days before Auditor General meeting about inflated procurement. Sam Mraiche gave Oilers tickets to 5 cabinet members, profited $300K flipping land to government. RCMP investigation launched.
stories.connection: Provincial accountability — Alberta. Connected to procurement analysis pipeline.

stories.title: FITAA Commissioner Named — Act Still Unproclaimed
stories.summary: Anton Boegman (former BC Chief Electoral Officer) named as FITAA Commissioner. Act STILL not proclaimed. Commissioner cannot begin work until act is in force, regulations finalized, and office established. CIJA lobbied both required ministers within 18 days of Gazette publication.
stories.connection: Direct update to Criminal Code finding (s.126 disobeying statute). FITAA non-proclamation is Finding #30.
